# Buried Answer

Do not demand conclusion-first writing. Find a separate passage that delays this response while discussing something else. Distinguish what bears on the answer from the author's preparation for writing it. An opening promise or vague verdict is adequate only when it supplies the operative answer the task requires. Useful reasoning elsewhere leaves an unrelated detour intact. Preserve purposeful instruction and narration. Missing answers belong elsewhere. Generalize across wording and topics.

## Hit

Did the Thornbury Lane protected cycle track cut collisions?

Ward councillor Delia Marsh asked the transport team this question at the September scrutiny meeting, and this note sets out what we found.

**Getting the figures took longer than expected. The council does not hold collision records itself; they come from the police, and the regional force moved its road traffic data to a new portal in June. Our existing data-sharing agreement referred to the old system, so legal services had to issue a variation, which the force's information governance unit countersigned on 19 August. The first extract we received covered the wrong ward boundary, because the portal still uses the pre-2023 boundaries, and a second request had to be raised with a hand-drawn polygon around the corridor. That extract arrived on 2 October as a spreadsheet with dates in American format, which our analyst, Tom Reyes, converted and checked line by line against the paper log kept by the road safety officer.**

We compared the 18 months before construction began (September 2022 to February 2024) with the 18 months after the track opened (April 2024 to September 2025), and counted only collisions within 20 metres of the Thornbury Lane carriageway.

On that basis, yes: injury collisions involving people on bikes fell from 11 to 4, and none of the four was classed as serious, against three serious in the earlier period. The fall is not explained by fewer riders. The automatic counter at the Elm Road bridge recorded an average of 1,140 cycle trips a weekday before the scheme and 1,570 after, a rise of 38 percent, so the collision rate per trip dropped by roughly three quarters.

Three of the four remaining collisions happened at the Mill Street junction, where the track ends and riders rejoin general traffic for about 60 metres. The team recommends that the planned extension to Mill Street be brought forward from the 2027 programme, and that a temporary advance stop line be painted there this winter at an estimated cost of 4,200 pounds.

## No-Hit

Our squeeze filter slowed to a drip on day three of the Bowron Lakes circuit. Is it finished?

That was the question I was asking myself on a beach at Isaac Lake last August, with four people and one filter, so here is how I worked it out. The answer depends on which of two things happened to it.

A hollow-fibre filter fails in two ways. It can clog, which slows the flow but leaves it safe, or it can freeze while wet, which cracks fibres and lets water through untreated, sometimes faster than before. So the first thing I checked was the overnight low. Our thermometer clip had read 4 degrees at dawn, the bottles inside the tent had not iced, and the filter had spent both nights in the bottom of my sleeping bag stuff sack. That made freezing unlikely, though not impossible, so I kept going.

Next I looked at the water. From Unna Lake onwards we had been filling where the river enters, and the water there was cloudy grey with glacial flour. Silt that fine passes straight into the fibres and packs them. Then I backflushed with the syringe, using clean filtered water, three full pushes. What came out was the same grey colour, and afterwards the flow went from about one drip a second back to a thin steady stream. A cracked filter would not have improved like that, and it would not have been pushing silt back out.

So no, it was not finished. It was clogged with glacial silt, and the backflush brought it most of the way back. For the rest of the trip we let water settle in a pot for twenty minutes, poured off the top through a bandana, and only then filtered it. We backflushed every evening, and the flow held for the remaining four days.

If yours might have frozen, treat it as broken until you can test it at home. The usual check is to blow air through the clean side while the filter sits in water and watch for a steady stream of bubbles, which means damaged fibres. On the trail, carry purification tablets as the backup.

## Hit

Did the revised loading schedule reduce missed collections?

The warehouse manager asked for a comparison before renewing the Saturday transport contract. This note covers the first twelve weeks under the revised loading schedule and the twelve weeks immediately before it.

**I started by looking for dispatch sheets on the shared drive. They had moved during the spring reorganization, and the person who knew their location was covering a trade show in Hamburg. Her automatic reply directed me to an assistant who had left the company. Once I obtained access, the files opened in a discontinued application. Our IT contractor converted them on a spare laptop while I checked parcel labels against photographs from the loading bay. I rebuilt the headings and sent a draft to three colleagues. One replied from holiday with a scan of a dispatch sheet pinned above her desk. We arranged a call, rescheduled it twice, and finally agreed on the column names on Thursday afternoon, before she left for the airport.**

For the comparison, a missed collection means a booked vehicle left without all parcels assigned to it. We counted scheduled departures rather than individual parcels, because parcel volume varies considerably between weekdays and Saturdays.

Yes. Missed collections fell from eighteen out of 120 scheduled departures to six out of 120. The number of parcels handled rose by nine percent over the same period, so the reduction accompanies higher throughput rather than a quieter warehouse.

Four of the remaining misses involved the late Saturday collection. Keep the revised weekday schedule, move Saturday packing forward by thirty minutes, and ask the carrier to confirm its arrival window in the renewed contract. Record the next twelve Saturdays separately so we can assess that remaining problem.

## No-Hit

Has the workshop label printer failed, or is the new workstation sending bad jobs?

The shipping team asked after three labels printed with missing barcodes. Replacing the printer would stop dispatch for a day, so I checked which part of the printing path could produce the fault before placing an order. These tests separate a damaged print mechanism from a bad instruction sent by the workstation.

The printer has two relevant ways to make a label. It can print its own diagnostic pattern from its front panel, or it can receive a label description from a computer. The diagnostic pattern bypasses the workstation, its driver, and the shipping application. If the same missing lines appeared there, a fault in the print head or its contact with the label stock would be a reasonable explanation.

I ran that pattern ten times using the roll already fitted. Every line was present and the printed barcodes scanned. Then I sent the same saved shipping label from the old workstation and the new one, alternating between them without touching the printer. All five old-workstation labels scanned. All five new-workstation labels lost the right edge of the barcode. Keeping the printer, stock, and file fixed isolates something in the new workstation's printing path.

Its driver was set to a label width of fifty millimetres, while the roll and old driver used sixty. Changing that setting restored the missing edge. I repeated the alternating test with ten labels from each workstation; all twenty scanned, including the three files that originally failed.

Keep the printer. The new workstation was clipping the label through its driver settings. Save the corrected width in the workstation setup instructions and print a diagnostic pattern plus a sample shipping label whenever another machine is connected. If either test fails, retain the failed labels before changing anything else so the next comparison remains useful.
